OTHER PRESENT:
 SRI C S HRITHWIK (SR PP)
 THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 13.02.2020, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 Crl.MC.No.889 OF 2020(A) 2  O R D E R Dated this the 13th day of February 2020 Petitioners are presently the directors of M/s Cochin Shipyard Employees Consumer Co-operative Society Ltd. No.E- 750.
They were nominated as directors vide Annexure II dated 18.8.2016.
It is seen that the sample in this case was collected by the Food Safety Officer on 28.07.2016 from A1.
The petitioners have been impleaded as accused Nos.12 and 13.
It is adequately clear that at the time of seizure they were not directors of the society.

2. A reading of Annexure 1 complaint does not indicate that petitioners were in any way responsible for the conduct of the business of the society as is required under Section 66 of the Food Saftety and Standards Act, 2006.

Merely being a director of a company or a society will not fasten the liability on the director unless there is a specific allegation and it is proved that they were responsible for the conduct of the business of the Company.

I find support in the decisions of National Small Industries Corpn. Ltd v. Harmeet Singh Paintal and Another [2010(2) KHC 355] and Rajagopalan P. v.
P.C.Jose and Another [2016(2) KHC 559].

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid submissions made by the learned counsel, I find that the prosecution as against petitioners, who are accused 12 and 13 in S.T. No.137/2019 on the files of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court (Economic Offences), Ernakulam is not sustainable and is accordingly quashed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
